verdict.rationale: GitLab's own docs confirm built-in CI/CD with pipelines ("Get started with GitLab CI/CD … Build and test your application", "SAST, DAST, and compliance in every pipeline"), and a community user calls the CI "truly great." The pack never explicitly documents defining pipelines as a config file in the repository or triggering them automatically on pushes and merge requests. Push-triggered runs appear only in a third-party Pulumi partner blurb, and a community report of CI workers not running concerns reliability rather than the capability itself. Missing for 10: first-party evidence of pipeline-as-code configuration stored in the repo, documented automatic triggers on push and merge request, and independent hands-on corroboration of those triggers.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define CI/CD pipelines as code in my repository and have them run automatically on pushes and pull requests

citations.quote: From planning to source control to CI/CD, everything you need to build and ship software faster in one platform.
SAST, DAST, and compliance in every pipeline.
The Pulumi integration with GitLab CI makes it easy to create and manage infrastructure stacks based on commits to specific Git branches so you can simply push-to-deploy your infrastructure.
